card.name: Verb right before a handling or missed-dose instruction
card.fires_on: Small verbs or linking words (is, may, of, prevent, reduce) in patient-instruction text, right before a word like missed, bleach, or a risk phrase. Most often the "is" after "If a dose of [drug]".

modes.label: Missed dose wording
modes.description: The word "is" after a dose or drug name, just before "missed".

modes.label: Application or swallowing precautions
modes.description: A verb or percent sign in topical or oral-use instructions, ahead of an effect or precaution.
modes.example: Wash hands after application as Adapalene and Benzoyl Peroxide Topical Gel, 0.3%/2.5<<%>> may bleach hair or colored fabrics.

card.plain: It marks the spot in dosing instructions where the next word is likely to be "missed" or an effect to avoid.
